errors.english: no downfall is incurred even if they are distributed and worn from that point forward
errors.why: de tshun chad means 'before that [time]' and bgos is 'distributed', not 'worn': there is no offence even if they are distributed before the robe-season ends.

note: A careful rendering of the Vinaya commentary on emergency robes and the kaṭhina periods; one doubtful phrase on the timing of distribution.

errors.english: Even if an object is conceived in one way, it merely conforms to a single intended object.
errors.why: The gang gis clause depends on the denied 'fixed nature' of sounds (there is no nature BY WHICH a sound would follow only one intended meaning), but the English asserts it as fact.

note: The anti-Mīmāṃsā argument is followed well overall; one relative clause is detached from the negation that governs it.

errors.english: two types based on consequence and essential nature through commitment
errors.why: The two kinds of inference from acceptance rest on a conceptually constructed (brtags pa) effect-reason and nature-reason; 'bras bu is 'effect' (as the following lines make clear), not 'consequence', and brtags pa is dropped.

errors.english: In this context, "perception and so forth" refers to the means of knowledge.
errors.why: The lemma glossed is 'de la' ('among those'), which the commentator identifies as perception and the rest; the English makes 'perception' the lemma.

errors.english: If the excluded is not a thesis according to the (pramāṇas) valid means of knowledge
errors.why: The pramāṇas are the instrument of refutation: 'if what is refuted by the pramāṇas themselves is not a thesis', not a thesis 'according to' them.

note: The pakṣa/pakṣābhāsa discussion is broadly followed, but the typology of inference from acceptance and some lemma glosses are muddled.

errors.english: As for the phrase "that is," it refers to the nature of the cause.
errors.why: The side opens by identifying the root-text words 'or if incomplete' as stating that even in its absence there is no contradiction; this is not rendered.

errors.english: Because the preceding tactile sensation of coldness functions as a cooperative condition for fire
errors.why: The commentary has just glossed the co-operating factor as fire: the prior cold touch has fire as its co-factor, not the reverse.

errors.english: the distinction is a contradiction without obstruction
errors.why: srod pa is read here for sdod pa ('remaining, enduring', cf. sdod pa'i phyogs on the next side): the alternative explains contradiction without the cause enduring, not 'without obstruction'.

note: A dense lemma-by-lemma commentary on the opposition of fire and cold; the gist is there but the causal roles and several lemmas are confused.
A faithful rendering of the commentary on consent-bearers and detained monks at the poṣadha.

errors.english: ### Chapter Twenty-one: Examination of Coming into Being and Dissolution
errors.why: This is the closing colophon of chapter 21; the verses that follow begin chapter 22 (Examination of the Tathāgata), but the heading places them under chapter 21.

fix.find: ### Chapter Twenty-one: Examination of Coming into Being and Dissolution
fix.replace:
This concludes the twenty-first chapter, the Examination of Coming into Being and Dissolution.

### Chapter Twenty-two

errors.english: then he would be a basis for them now; but since he depends on them, he is contingent upon that dependence.
errors.why: MMK 22.6: such a Tathāgata would only now come to depend on (appropriate) the aggregates, and having depended would then come to be; he is not a basis for them.

fix.find: then he would be a basis for them now; but since he depends on them, he is contingent upon that dependence.
fix.replace: then he would only now come to depend on them, and having depended on them, he would thereby come to be.

errors.english: At the time of nirvana [note: original: "mya ngan 'das pa"], the chain of existence is severed because the continuity of becoming has been completely stilled.
errors.why: The root verses of the Mūlamadhyamakakārikā are rendered as running prose, and this line, a reductio consequence (annihilation would follow at nirvāṇa), reads as an assertion.

note: The MMK 21.17-22.8 verses are mostly rendered correctly in prose, but the chapter division is misplaced and verse 22.6 is misconstrued.

errors.english: That which is invisible but causes these practices is called Dharma
errors.why: The unseen force (adṛṣṭa) produced by these practices is called dharma; the practices cause it, not the reverse, and adṛṣṭa as a technical term is lost.

errors.english: Substances are the actions of substance
errors.why: The Vaiśeṣika rule is that substances produce (bya ba, kārya) another substance, parallel to qualities producing qualities; 'actions' confuses it with karman.
In this Vaiśeṣika list dbang bskur ba renders abhiṣecana, ritual ablution/consecration, not a tantric empowerment.

note: A sound rendering of a Buddhist exposition of Vaiśeṣika categories, with a few doctrinal terms off.

errors.english: appears connected with interrupting the term "non-annihilation"
errors.why: bar du gcod pa here means the terms are connected across intervening words (separated yet linked in meaning), not that one 'interrupts' the other.

note: The Prajñāpāramitā dialogue and the commentary on the order of the negations are rendered faithfully apart from one obscure phrase.
A faithful rendering of the commentary on the bath-powder and lake similes of the first and second dhyāna.

errors.english: Who else shall receive the supreme dust of your feet upon their heads, where even the gods bowed their finest limbs with faith?
errors.why: The verse laments that even he, the dust of whose feet was supreme on the heads the gods bowed in faith, has perished; it is not a question about who will receive the dust.

errors.english: toward this world that possesses your knowledge and love
errors.why: mkhyen brtser ldan ('possessed of wisdom and love') addresses the Buddha, not the world: 'why have you, wise and loving one, become indifferent to this world?'

errors.english: Hero, because we are separated from you
errors.why: The word completes mgon po ('Protector') from the previous side, and the subject who wanders is the world blinded by ignorance; it is not 'Hero'.

errors.english: Alas! The wealth of virtues accumulated over ten million (kalpas) aeons has been seized by the Lord of Death.
errors.why: The lament is in quatrains of verse, and it is rendered as running prose throughout.

note: A readable version of the lament on the Buddha's parinirvāṇa, but it is set as prose and misreads several epithets and the closing verse.
